subject: Chemistry
description: Reactivity series, alloy compositions, everyday metal uses

questions.stem: The MOST reactive metal in the reactivity series (from those commonly tested) is:
questions.explanation: Reactivity series (most → least reactive): K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > [H] > Cu > Ag > Au > Pt. Potassium reacts violently with water. Gold and platinum are the least reactive (noble metals).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Match the ALLOY with its MAIN COMPOSITION. A. Brass.  B. Bronze.  C. Stainless Steel.  D. Solder. List-II: 1. Copper + Zinc.  2. Copper + Tin.  3. Iron + Chromium + Nickel.  4. Tin + Lead.
questions.explanation: Brass (Cu + Zn). Bronze (Cu + Sn — classical Bronze-Age material). Stainless Steel (Fe + Cr + Ni — typically 18% Cr + 8% Ni for '18/8'). Solder (Sn + Pb — modern lead-free uses Sn + Ag). Other alloys: duralumin (Al + Cu + Mg + Mn), gunmetal (Cu + Sn + Zn).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: Lithium — lightest metal (density 0.53 g/cc). Li-ion batteries. Used in lubricants, aircraft alloys. Aluminium (2.7) is the lightest COMMON construction metal. Magnesium (1.74), Sodium (0.97) are also very light. Densest metal: Osmium (22.6).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The metal used in making MAGNETS is:
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic metals: Iron (Fe), Cobalt (Co), Nickel (Ni), Gadolinium. Most common in everyday magnets: iron + alloys (Alnico: Al+Ni+Co+Fe), neodymium (NdFeB), samarium-cobalt. Copper/silver — diamagnetic / paramagnetic, not permanent magnets.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The ONLY non-metal that is LIQUID at room temperature is:
questions.explanation: Bromine (Br₂) — only LIQUID non-metal at room temperature (reddish-brown liquid, MP −7 °C, BP 59 °C). Iodine is solid (sublimes). Sulphur is yellow solid. Mercury (Hg) is the only LIQUID METAL at room temperature.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: STEEL becomes STAINLESS when alloyed with:
questions.explanation: Stainless Steel = Fe + C (≤2%) + Cr (≥10.5%, typically 16-18%) + Ni (for austenitic grades, 8-10%). Cr forms a passive oxide layer that resists corrosion. Named grades: 304, 316 (marine). 18/8 stainless = 18% Cr + 8% Ni.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The metal with the HIGHEST electrical and thermal conductivity is:
questions.explanation: Silver — highest electrical AND thermal conductivity of any metal. Expensive, so COPPER is preferred in everyday electrical wiring (next best). Silver is used in high-end electronics, RF connectors, antibacterial coatings. Gold — least reactive + good conductor, used where corrosion resistance matters.
